newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya bourse regulator in agreement with Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Kenya bourse regulator in agreement with Malaysia.

text.p: Kenyan and Malaysian capital markets regulators signed a bilateral agreement on Monday aimed at improving the efficiency of the Nairobi bourse.

The Capital Markets Authority of Kenya (CMA) and the Securities Commission of Malaysia signed a Memorandum of Understanding that would facilitate the exchange of information on how to establish the minimum standards required for an efficient market.

"Kenya stands to benefit from drawing on the experience of Malaysia on various issues relating to capital markets development -- especially in nurturing the emergence of new market institutions and new products," Paul Melly, chief executive of the CMA said.
He added that the Rating Agency of Malaysia would also act as a role model for the establishment of a similar institution in Kenya.
The agreement will also involve technical assistance and training of Kenyans to learn firsthand at the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in Malaysia.
The Nairobi bourse has a market capitalisation of $2.28 billion and is ranked the fifth in Africa after after the stock exchanges of South Africa, Egypt, Nigeria and Ghana.
